_doc: Purpose: drafting-standard profile for the ISO system, consumed by cadcore.i18n.standards (projection angle plus sheet/line/lettering/title-block conventions). Background: standard-dependent values must live in data rather than code branches, and any field whose standard text was not obtained stays null and is listed in na_fields, so 'not fetched' can never masquerade as a real value; no standard text is reproduced here (R3).

source.retrieval_method: read-only fetch of public web pages (HTTP status recorded per URL); standard bodies are paywalled and none of their text is copied into this file

projection_angle_evidence.shows: Not readable from this network on the retrieval date (bot protection), so the ISO standard body could not be checked at clause level at all.

projection_angle_evidence.publisher: TU Darmstadt, Institute for Machine Elements and Machine Design (public German technical university tutorial)
projection_angle_evidence.shows: States that the ISO/DIN-family projection standard offers two methods and that the sheet carries the symbol that declares which one applies; the page assigns method 1 to Germany and most of Europe and method 3 to the USA, i.e. the ISO family itself is not presented as mandating a single default (paraphrase).

projection_angle_evidence.publisher: IDEA Technology (Japanese engineering firm), JIS drawing-standards article series
projection_angle_evidence.shows: Conflicting public secondary account: the same page calls third-angle standard for ISO in one section and first-angle standard in Europe in another, so it cannot settle the ISO default either way. The server answered HTTP 500 while still serving the article.
projection_angle_evidence.grade: public secondary source, low-grade and self-contradicting on this point

source.na_policy: null means not fetched (-1), never 'zero'; here projection_angle is null because the reachable public evidence says the ISO family permits both first-angle and third-angle and lets the projection symbol on the sheet decide, while the official catalogue page was unreadable (403). Guessing a default would be worse than reporting NA, because callers must show the ambiguity rather than silently mirror a drawing.
notes: na_fields lists exactly the null-valued fields, in contract order: a gate can assert set(na_fields) == {k for k, v in profile.items() if v is None}.

This is the only profile whose projection_angle is null: cadcore.i18n.standards.projection_angle_for('iso') therefore returns None and the caller has to handle the NA case explicitly, which is the intended contract behaviour.
All numeric tables remain null because ISO bodies are paywalled; no value is copied from memory or from the DIN profile.
